blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets on your Mac

Google Sheets is a web-based tool. It does not have a native Mac installer. You should use Google Chrome for the most reliable experience. Other browsers like Safari often struggle with complex sheets.

To make it feel like a desktop app, open your sheet in Chrome. Click the three-dot menu at the top right. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Then click Install page as app. This creates a dedicated window for your compensation data.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for compensation analysts
Speed is vital when you manage large salary datasets. Stop clicking through menus. Use these shortcuts to move faster in your browser.

You likely handle sensitive pay equity data and market benchmarks. Keep your sheets clean to avoid errors. Always freeze your top row so your headers stay visible while you scroll. This is a basic but necessary step for data integrity.
Use filters to isolate specific job families or regions. This helps you focus on one segment of your salary structure at a time. It prevents you from accidentally editing the wrong cell.
How Lazur helps your compensation workflow
Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen when you hold ⌥ ⌘. It listens when you hold fn. It does not click buttons for you, but it acts as a guide to keep your focus on the task.
When you are stuck, ask Lazur to walk you through a process. It can point at menu items or explain how to use a specific function. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your data.

Many analysts spend hours fixing manual errors. If your compensation planning process takes too long, check your version history. Use [See revision history in Google Sheets](/how-to/see-revision-history-in-google-sheets) to track changes. This ensures you know who changed a salary band and why.

Do not rely on memory for complex formulas. Keep a dedicated tab for documentation. Explain your logic there. If you need to share your work, use [Share with view only access in Google Sheets](/how-to/share-with-view-only-access-in-google-sheets) to prevent unauthorized edits.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Sheets is a web-based app. You should use Chrome and create a shortcut to run it in its own window.

faq.question: How do I see all keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / while inside your spreadsheet. A menu will appear with every available shortcut.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my spreadsheet files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It guides you, answers your questions, and helps you dictate text.

faq.question: Why is my Google Sheet running slowly?
faq.answer: You might be hitting the 20 million cell limit or have too many active collaborators. Try clearing unused cells or splitting your data into smaller files.
